quantisation_bound: 5 mm per axis (1 cm position quantum, round-to-nearest); Euclidean <= 8.7 mm; exact against the quantised truth at every delivered tick
notes: The emitter owns the canon (10,000 seeded objects: random walks, circular orbits and a few fast movers) and a 10 m spatial hash. At each delivery it intersects the subscriber's moving interest region (a sphere or a perspective frustum) with the hash and sends only the difference from what that subscriber already has: objects that entered the region (absolute quantised pose), objects that left (id only), and objects whose pose moved (a quantised delta). Positions are quantised to a 1 cm grid (round-to-nearest), so a reconstruction is off by at most 5 mm per axis (8.7 mm Euclidean) and never drifts, because the delta is always taken against the quantised truth. Deltas travel as biased fixed-width bit fields whose width is chosen per axis from the 90th percentile of |delta|, with outliers escaping into a varint list, and the changed set travels as a bitmap over the subscriber's previous set when that is smaller than the id list. The motion channel carries each object's velocity in 1/64 quantum per tick; the emitter stays viewpoint-agnostic and the projector converts it into its own frame (and into optical flow) locally, which is what lets it predict between deliveries. Every packet carries since_version, so a late joiner or a subscriber that lost a packet is detected and resynchronised from a keyframe (full region, absolute poses) and rebuilds the emitter's ground truth exactly. The emitter is single threaded and serves the 64 subscribers on their own cadences (2-60 Hz, staggered); 9471363 delivered states were compared against the ground truth and 0 mismatched.
